ground_truth_note: The claim that cooked rice must be thrown out after 24 hours is inaccurate. According to the USDA and food safety experts, cooked rice is safe to eat for 3 to 4 days if it is refrigerated promptly and stored properly. http://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/leftovers-and-food-safety
note_text: The post expresses a personal belief ("I never knew...") about a 24-hour rule for rice disposal. While this is overly cautious compared to official guidelines (USDA recommends 3-4 days for refrigerated cooked rice), the post is sharing a conservative food safety approach rather than making a definitively false factual claim that causes harm. The 24-hour timeframe, while unnecessarily strict, errs on the side of caution for food safety. Correcting this could potentially encourage less safe food handling practices. The core principle (cooked rice doesn't last indefinitely and should be discarded after a period of time) is valid - only the specific timeframe is more conservative than necessary.
search_results:
**No, you do not have to throw out cooked rice after exactly 24 hours.** Multiple sources contradict this claim, stating that properly refrigerated cooked rice lasts **3–6 days** depending on the type and guidelines.[1][2][3]

**Detailed storage guidelines from sources:**
- Cooked brown rice can last **4–6 days** in the fridge when cooled quickly and stored in airtight containers.[1][https://www.chicorice.com/blogs/all-about-rice/how-to-store-brown-rice]
- Cooked rice (all types) keeps for **3–4 days** (up to a week per some claims) in the refrigerator, or up to 8 months frozen.[2][https://www.healthline.com/nutrition/does-rice-go-bad]
- USDA recommends consuming refrigerated cooked rice within **3–4 days** to limit bacterial growth like Bacillus cereus; freezer storage extends to months.[3][https://www.mill.com/blog/does-rice-expire]

**Key food safety note:** Refrigerate cooked rice within 2 hours of cooking to minimize risks; discard if it smells off, shows mold, or changes texture.[2][3] No source supports a strict 24-hour rule.
